# Recipe — add a screen

**Use when:** the game needs a new full-screen destination the scene service can navigate to.
**Do not** hand-create the scene, and do not copy an existing screen folder (rule #13).

## 1. Edit the manifest

`Tools/Codegen/Manifests/game.scenes.json` — append one entry:

```json
{ "id": "Shop", "order": 2, "screenClass": "ShopScreen", "address": "Scenes/Shop", "paramType": "ShopParam" }
```

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `id` | The `SceneKey` name. PascalCase, unique. |
| `order` | Next free integer. |
| `screenClass` | Conventionally `<id>Screen`. The scope class name is derived as `<screenClass>Scope`. |
| `address` | Always `Scenes/<id>` — the address the scene service loads. |
| `paramType` | The typed navigation parameter record, conventionally `<id>Param`. |

## 2. Run the scaffold

```
Framework/Scaffold/Sync        (editor menu)
```

Scaffold.Sync is idempotent: existing files are left alone, only what is missing is created.

## 3. What lands

| Path | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Assets/<Sku>/Scenes/Shop.unity` | scaffold | From the framework `Screen.scenetemplate`. Required node: `WorldRoot`. |
| `Assets/<Sku>/Features/Shop/Presentation/ShopScreen.cs` | **you** | Stub, generate-once. Extends `ScreenBase`, `namespace Game.Presentation`. |
| `Assets/<Sku>/Features/Shop/Composition/ShopScreenScope.cs` | **you** | Stub, `namespace Game.Composition`. Scaffold.Sync **attaches this to the scene's `Scope` node** — boot's `SceneScopeFactory` throws without it. |
| `Assets/<Sku>/Features/Shop/Application/ShopParam.cs` | **you** | Stub, a record, `namespace Game.Application`. |
| `…/{Presentation,Composition,Application}/Game.<Layer>.asmref` | Scaffold | Three lines each, generate-once. They are what puts the three files in three assemblies. |

> **One screen spans three assemblies, and that is the point.** The screen decides *what happens*
> (Presentation), the scope *wires it* (Composition — the only SKU tier that may name a container),
> and the param is *engine-free data* the screen ctor-injects (Application, so it lands in the
> headless gate for free). It is also why a single per-manifest output directory could never have
> worked, and why the stubs carry a `{{Namespace}}` token instead of a literal.
| `Assets/<Sku>/Gen/SceneKeys.gen.cs` | codegen | Gains `SceneKeys.Shop`. Never hand-edit. |
| The Addressables entry for `Scenes/Shop` | scaffold | Part of the four-legs check. |

## 4. Write the controller

`ShopScreen` extends `ScreenBase` — a **plain ctor-injected C# class, never a `MonoBehaviour`**.
Override only the legs you need; all seven default to no-ops:

`OnLoadAsync(ct)` · `OnEnter()` · `OnPause()` · `OnResume()` · `OnExit()` · `OnUnloadAsync(ct)` ·
`OnBackRequested()`

The controller decides **what happens**. Its View (in `Assets/<Sku>/Views/`) decides only **how it
looks**, and must pass both View tests (`AGENTS.framework.md` §3).

> A View renders under a **render-layer host** (`GetHost`), not under `WorldRoot` — and that parent
> is decided **per object**, never once for the screen (rule #16). Screen furniture anchored to an
> edge or the safe area goes under the host of the layer that owns it — `Ui` for the screen's own
> furniture, `Popup` for dialog chrome, `Overlay` for system overlays
> ([`add-widget.md`](./add-widget.md)); only something anchored in the game's own space *and*
> drawing through a `Renderer` goes under `WorldRoot`
> ([`add-world-object.md`](./add-world-object.md)). Orientation comes from the
> serialized `CanvasCameraFitter._referenceResolution` — no framework edit needed. Set the TMP font
> explicitly; the templates ship it empty so no consumer font GUID is baked into a package asset.

## 5. Gate

```sh
Tools/Build/pf-build.sh codegen --check     # SceneKeys is regenerated
Framework/Scaffold/Check                    # four legs: manifest ↔ scene ↔ Addressables ↔ class
```

Both must be green. `Framework/Doctor` check 6 runs the same drift gate.

**Visual finish (rule #17).** A screen the player sees ships finished, not as a wireframe: walk the
eight-point checklist in the `pf-visual-design` skill and take a capture at FHD in the SKU's own
orientation (1080x1920 portrait, 1920x1080 landscape — never the tool's default).
Follow `docs/art-direction.md` if the artist wrote one; otherwise you decide, and record the choice as
design tokens.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| `SceneKeys.Shop` does not compile | Codegen not run — the manifests live outside `Assets/`, so editing one raises no Unity import event. |
| `SceneScopeFactory` throws at boot | The `<screenClass>Scope` component is not attached to the scene's `Scope` node. Re-run `Scaffold.Sync`. |
| Four-legs check names a missing Addressables entry | The scene asset exists but was never addressed. Re-run `Scaffold.Sync`; do not add the entry by hand. |
| The screen loads but nothing is clickable | The render-layer host canvas is missing its own `GraphicRaycaster` (`architecture-map.md` §5). |
